readingA.label: A defect
readingA.text: Tradition holds a toilet spoils the East, the sun's quarter.

readingB.label: Acceptable in one strip
readingB.text: The 16-zone school divides the East more finely and allows a toilet in the strip nearest the South-East.

readingA.label: Not ideal
readingA.text: The North belongs to Kubera, lord of wealth. Tradition reads it as water, unsuited to the kitchen's fire.

readingB.label: Not ideal, not a fault
readingB.text: Modern practice calls a northern kitchen less than best, not a fault to correct.

title: The main bedroom in the West

readingA.label: Acceptable
readingA.text: Tradition accepts the West, the other settled, heavier quarter, instead of the South-West.

readingB.label: Advised against
readingB.text: The 16-zone school keeps the main bedroom out of the west-south-west, its quarter of study.

title: A front door in the South-East

readingA.label: Acceptable in the right position
readingA.text: The 32 named door positions sort good from bad within the South-East. Exact position, not direction, decides.

readingB.label: A defect
readingB.text: The Manasara, a classical Vastu treatise, says a home should never face the South-East.

title: Which way to sleep with your head

readingA.label: Head to the South is best
readingA.text: Tradition ranks head-to-South first, East next, West neutral.

readingB.label: Avoid head to the North
readingB.text: The one point every school agrees on. We pass it on as tradition, claiming nothing about your health.

readingA.label: Against the West or South-West wall
readingA.text: Classically, idols stand against the West or South-West wall, so the worshipper faces East.

readingB.label: Against the East wall
readingB.text: Modern practice often stands them against the East wall, facing West.

readingA.label: The sources contradict each other
readingA.text: The North, North-West and South-East are each insisted on by serious sources.

readingB.label: Too sharp to rule on
readingB.text: Choosing one would invent a tradition. We report it as not checked unless you say where yours is.

title: A road pointing straight at the plot

readingA.label: It depends which direction
readingA.text: A road from the North-East, North or East is harmless. From the South, South-West, South-East or North-West comes the thrust tradition warns of.

readingB.label: Always harmful
readingB.text: The strict school treats any such road as a wound, from any direction.

readingA.label: A North-East extension is welcome
readingA.text: Tradition reads a North-East extension as a good sign, not a fault.

readingB.label: Every extension is a fault
readingB.text: The strict school treats anything that sticks out as a fault, the North-East included.

title: Where the prayer room belongs

readingA.label: Classical — the centre
readingA.text: The family deity holds the centre of the home, as the Manasara sets out.

readingB.label: Modern — the North-East
readingB.text: Near-universal modern practice places the prayer room in the North-East.

howWeScore: Your score follows the modern reading: North-East ideal, North and East acceptable. No position counts as a defect, the classical centre included. The other school's advice never becomes a fault.
